text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The presidential palace and right-wing Disy look at ways to forge closer ties with centre-right Diko after its president's comments of shaky relations between the two parties.
- Greek Education Minister Gerrasimos Arsenis causes a political incident by attacking federation as an accepted solution to the Cyprus problem.
- Cyprus is expected to pay its first instalment for the S-300 missiles in early February.
- Turkey pledges military backing for Turkish Cypriots.
- Greece and Cyprus agree on education co-operation.
- Arsenis's position on the accepted form of a Cyprus solution prompts questions.
- Relations between co-governing parties Disy and Diko hang in the balance.
- The Central Bank is committed to deregulating foreign investments, says its governor.
- Diko leader Spyros Kyprianou warns the government pact could disolve by the end of the week unless he gets assurances that relations between his party and government partner Disy will improve.
